faq.q: What is a titanium derailleur limit screw?
faq.a: A titanium derailleur limit screw is a precision-machined derailleur hardware component used in front/rear derailleur h/l limit adjustment screw. Manufactured from Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V for optimal strength, corrosion resistance, and weight savings.

faq.q: What torque should I use for titanium derailleur limit screw?
faq.a: Recommended installation torque depends on thread size and lubrication. For M5 titanium fasteners: 4-5 Nm (dry), 3-4 Nm (with anti-seize). Always use titanium-compatible anti-seize compound to prevent galling (cold welding) of threads.

faq.q: How is titanium derailleur limit screw manufactured?
faq.a: Titanium Derailleur Limit Screw is manufactured using Cold heading. Critical process controls include tool path optimization, coolant temperature management, and dimensional verification at each operation.

faq.q: What is the most common issue with titanium derailleur limit screw?
faq.a: The most common issue is surface contamination from iron pickup during machining requiring acid passivation (astm f86). Mitigation includes proper process control, material certification, and adherence to recommended installation procedures and torque values.
